summary:
Denmark permits legal gender recognition by self-declaration since 1 September 2014. A person over 18 changes registered sex by stating the wish and completing a six-month reflection period, without medical evaluation, psychiatric diagnosis, surgery or sterilization. Parliament adopted that removal of diagnosis and surgery requirements in June 2014 by 59 votes to 52.

Danish passports are issued with male, female and X sex descriptors, so a non-binary holder can carry a travel document that records neither male nor female.

Discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics is prohibited. The Equal Treatment Act covers sexual orientation and gender identity in employment and services. The 1996 Act on Prohibition of Unequal Treatment in the Labor Market lists sexual orientation, and a 2015 court ruling in a claim by a transgender woman against a former employer held that gender identity or expression is covered. Workplace protection on gender identity is recorded as in place since 2015, with fair-housing protection on gender identity recorded throughout the period, and complaints are considered by the Board of Equal Treatment established under the 2008 Act.

Additional penalties for crimes motivated by sexual orientation have applied since 2004 amendments to the Penal Code. The sources do not record the hate-crime penalty provision as expressly covering gender identity or expression.

Freedom from arbitrary arrest on grounds of gender identity is recorded as affirmed in every year from 2011 to 2024.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 15 June 2012, including marriage in the Church of Denmark, following registered partnership since 1 October 1989. A visitor travelling with a same-sex spouse is therefore travelling under a gender-neutral marriage law.

On 10 September 2024 the Supreme Court held that placement of a trans inmate to serve in a men’s prison department is not a violation of human rights. That ruling is the leading Danish authority on trans placement in custody and indicates the placement risk in detention.

The UN Committee against Torture in its 8th periodic review found that some trans people, QTIBIPOC people and migrants reported denial of access to spaces and services and threats. The Danish Institute for Human Rights LGBT+ barometer records that 38 percent of homosexual and bisexual respondents report differential treatment based on gender, sexual orientation or appearance, and that hate speech targeting sexual orientation, gender identity or expression or sex characteristics recurs annually.

In the period covered by the ILGA-Europe Annual Review 2025, a migrant trans woman was murdered in July in a hotel room in Copenhagen.

Access to gender-affirming care in Denmark is gatekept and slow. Patients seeking hormone therapy report being required to present in ways reflecting stereotypical gender roles, with trans men describing a need to give male-coded answers, after several psychological sessions. Recorded adult waits are generally 11 to 16 months for hormone therapy and 4 to 6 years for bottom surgery, which leads many trans adults to seek care abroad. A visitor should not expect timely access to hormones or surgery in country.

There is no ban on conversion therapy. A bill was revived in August 2026, but no prohibition was in force in the sources.

In February 2013 a Guatemalan trans woman, Fernanda Milan, became the first transgender person granted asylum in Denmark on grounds of persecution for gender identity and trans activism, citing police attacks and threats. She was initially refused, was placed in a facility for men where she was sexually assaulted several times, and authorities reopened the case when she established that return would endanger her life.
tangentialFactors:
Anti-trans discourse intensified while Parliament debated lowering the age limit for legal gender recognition. The sources record the intensification and the debate but do not record a change to the over-18 rule.

Denmark removed gender identity disorder from the National Board of Health list of mental illnesses with effect on 1 January 2017, after a 2016 parliamentary decision. Denmark was the second country after France in 2010 to take that step, before the World Health Organization in June 2018 replaced the diagnosis with gender incongruence classified as a sexual health condition.

Openly transgender soldiers serve in all branches of the Danish Defence without hindrance, and discrimination in recruitment, placement and promotion is prohibited.

The Committee against Torture urged psychosocial counselling and remedy for intersex persons. In March in the period covered by the 2025 review, Denmark signed a UN resolution against intersex discrimination.

Among LGBTI students aged 15 to 25, 40 percent reported self-harm in the past year, at two to three times the rate of classmates. The finding describes resident youth health rather than visitor law, but it indicates strain in the school climate.
localsOnly:
Transgender health care for minors became more restricted under 2023 guidelines. Puberty blockers are recommended at Tanner stage two or three to allow further exploration. For children under ten showing adequate signs of gender dysphoria, parents receive advisory information. For children over ten, the pathway requires at least five investigative interviews, psychiatric evaluation, information sessions on hormone therapy, and review of school and municipal records. Hormone consent is possible from age 15 without parental involvement. No surgical options are available until 18. Recorded possible barriers include psychosis and autism where dysphoria is deemed an aspect of mental illness, and history of abuse, self-harm and suicidal ideation.

Joint adoption by same-sex couples has been allowed since 1 July 2010, after stepchild adoption since 1999. Lesbian couples gained access to artificial insemination after Parliament voted on 2 June 2006 to repeal the ban, with the non-biological parent recorded on the birth certificate since 2013 for in vitro fertilization. In August 2024 the government announced a plan to strengthen multi-parent families with three to four parents.

In a 2019 workplace report, 69 percent of LGBT respondents were open about sexual orientation to colleagues and 9 percent felt they could not be open.
outOfScopeNotes:
Unresolved in the inventory is whether any national rule governs bathroom or facility access by gender identity, as no source states a provision.

Not sourced are trans-specific entry, visa or border-screening rules for Denmark, beyond the passport X marker and the 2013 asylum precedent.

Not sourced is enforcement data on how often the anti-discrimination and hate-crime provisions are applied or what penalties result in trans cases.

Unresolved is the outcome of the parliamentary debate on lowering the legal gender recognition age and the outcome of the conversion-therapy bill revived in August 2026.

Unresolved is the calendar year of the July hotel murder in Copenhagen as reported in the 2025 annual review, which the inventory records by month without a year.
